title: What Is the Ideal Humidity Level in a Home?
h1: What Is the Ideal Humidity Level in a Home?
description: Ideal indoor humidity is about 30 to 50 percent. Learn the signs your home is too damp or too dry and simple ways to keep humidity in a comfortable range.
quick_answer: For most homes, the ideal indoor humidity is between about 30 and 50 percent. That range feels comfortable, helps protect wood floors and furniture, and keeps mold and dust mites in check. Staying under 60 percent is the main goal in damp weather, while dropping below 30 percent can cause dry skin, static and irritated sinuses.
body:
Humidity is one of those things you don't notice until it's off. Too much and the house feels sticky and smells musty. Too little and your skin cracks, your nose dries out and the floors start to creak. In Southern California, you can see both in the same year, sometimes in the same week.

What happens when humidity is too high?

When indoor humidity stays above 60 percent for long stretches, you'll start to see problems:

  • Condensation on windows and cold surfaces
  • Mildew in bathrooms, closets and corners
  • Musty odors in carpet, upholstery and stored clothes
  • Dust mites, which thrive in damp air and trigger allergies
  • Peeling paint, swollen wood and warped doors
  • A cool but clammy feeling, even with the AC running

Coastal homes see this most during marine layer season, and homes that are closed up much of the day trap moisture from cooking, showers and laundry.

What happens when humidity is too low?

Below about 30 percent, dry air causes a different set of problems:

  • Dry skin, chapped lips and itchy eyes
  • Sore throats and nosebleeds, especially at night
  • Static shocks from carpets and doorknobs
  • Gaps in hardwood floors and cracks in wood furniture
  • Houseplants that dry out quickly

Santa Ana winds can push indoor humidity way down in a short time, and inland homes tend to run drier overall.

How do you measure humidity at home?

Pick up an inexpensive digital hygrometer. Many smart thermostats also show indoor humidity. Check a few rooms at different times of day. Bathrooms and kitchens will read higher during use, so the bedroom and living room give you a better baseline.

How do you bring humidity back into range?

To lower humidity

  1. Use exhaust fans. Run the bathroom fan during showers and for a while after, and use the range hood when cooking.
  2. Check the dryer vent. A disconnected or clogged vent can dump warm, wet air into the laundry room or attic.
  3. Run the AC. Air conditioning removes moisture as it cools. A properly sized system removes more than an oversized one that short-cycles.
  4. Fix leaks. Look under sinks, around water heaters and at the AC condensate line.
  5. Add a dehumidifier. A portable unit works for one room. A whole-home dehumidifier connects to your HVAC system and handles the entire house quietly.

To raise humidity

  1. Use a portable humidifier in bedrooms during dry spells. Clean it often so it doesn't grow mold or bacteria.
  2. Seal air leaks. Gaps around doors, windows and attic hatches let dry outside air in.
  3. Consider a whole-home humidifier. It adds moisture through your ductwork and is controlled by a humidistat, so you don't overdo it.
  4. Air-dry some laundry indoors or keep a few houseplants. Small sources add up.

Don't push humidity too high. Over 50 percent in a dry spell can lead to condensation on windows and walls, especially on cool nights.

Does the ideal range change with the seasons?

A little. In warm months, aim for the upper part of the range, around 45 to 50 percent, and keep it from climbing past 60. On cold nights, especially in inland homes, the lower half of the range, around 35 to 40 percent, helps avoid condensation on windows and outside walls. Watch your windows: if they fog up regularly on cool mornings, the indoor air is holding more moisture than it should for the weather.

Does humidity affect how warm or cool your home feels?

Yes. Damp air feels warmer in summer because sweat doesn't evaporate as easily, so you may set the thermostat lower than you need to. Dry air feels cooler in winter, so you may turn up the heat. Keeping humidity in the right range lets you be comfortable at more moderate settings, which is easier on your system and your energy bill.

faqs: Is 55 percent humidity too high indoors?

It's a little above the ideal range but not a problem for short periods. If your home sits at 55 percent or higher for weeks, especially with musty smells or condensation, take steps to bring it down.
What humidity is best for sleeping?
Most people sleep comfortably around 40 to 50 percent. That range helps prevent a dry throat and nose without making the room feel stuffy.
Can my HVAC system control humidity?
Your AC removes some moisture as it cools. For more control, a whole-home humidifier or dehumidifier can be added to most central systems and controlled by a humidistat or compatible thermostat.
